newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OVER 150,000/T CONCENTRATE MAROONED AT OK TEDI.
newsitem.headline: OVER 150,000/T CONCENTRATE MAROONED AT OK TEDI.

text.p: Copper concentrate stockpiles of over 150,000 tonnes from the Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea have been marooned due to severe drought conditions in the area, a spokesman for the mine said on Tuesday.

"Nothing is moving, the sky's are blue and it is very dry," the spokesman told Reuters. Mining of ore at the mine was continuing, although two mills used to produce concentrate, which is later smelted into cathode and other forms of semi-finished metal, have been closed because of the drought.

"There's plenty of concentrate stockpiled," the spokesman said. He said the concentrate was sitting idle in a slurry pipeline leading from the mine to Kiunga port on the Fly Riverat Kiunga or on barges laid up by the drought.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, which holds 52.6 percent of the mine, said earlier on Tuesday that in view of low inventories of diesel fuel, it had decided to shut down the mills and bring forward maintenance work.
Fuel to run the mills is normally ferried on the river barges on return journeys to Kiunga.
Mining of ore would proceed although there would be no concentrate production until the drought eased, the spokesman said.

This is the second time in about two months that shipments of concentrate from Ok Tedi have been suspended because of drought. In June, drought brought barge traffic on the Fly river to a halt for a month.
The spokesman said 1997 had been an unusually dry year for the region, which he attributed to the El Nino weather pattern.
The first mill was shut down last week and the second mill ceased operating on Monday.
Smelters which have supply contracts with Ok Tedi have been informed of the situation, the spokesman said.
"We're talking to them all the time, letting them know what's going on and to let them make other arrangements," he said.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese smelting pool consisting of seven Japanese smelting companies.
The other partners in the mine are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp, with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
Ok Tedi produces about 600,000 tonnes of concentrates a year.
